tasks.task_description: Determine the shape, size, and merging pattern of the area following a barrier toll plaza in which vehicles fan in from B tollbooth egress lanes (B > L) down to L travel lanes, for a highway with L lanes per direction. The design must incorporate accident prevention, throughput (vehicles per hour at the point where the plaza joins the L outgoing lanes), and cost (land and road construction). The problem asks for the optimal design, not a performance analysis of an existing one, and requires a light/heavy traffic performance comparison, an autonomous-vehicle (AV) mix analysis, and an analysis of the effect of the proportion of conventional, exact-change, and electronic tollbooths.
tasks.task_analysis: Assumptions. (1) Per the expert consultation (Exchange 1), the problem text does not settle whether the three considerations combine lexicographically or as a weighted sum, nor who chooses the weights; the model therefore adopts a lexicographic objective: minimize total paved fan-in area (length times mean width, proxying land and pavement cost) subject to two hard constraints — (T) exit throughput: booth-queue utilization rho < 1 and exit demand per lane not exceeding the HCM lane capacity anchor of 2,200 veh/h/ln, so that no queue spills back into the fan-in; and (S) merge-point capacity: at every merge stage, the number of simultaneous merges m_k does not exceed the bound derived from the per-point merge capacity. (2) The fan-in is confined to a bounded corridor at the barrier egress width; only its length is a free design variable. (3) Each vehicle merges at most once, into the nearest surviving lane. (4) Stages are staggered longitudinally by a minimum spacing dx_min = 2 s of travel at the 65 mph free-flow speed (HCM typical design FFS). (5) Booth arrivals are stochastic, modeled as an M/M/c queue (c = B booths, service rate determined by the booth-type mix); light traffic is 40% of the L-lane capacity, heavy traffic is 95% of capacity. (6) AVs are an ETC-class (non-stop) subpopulation whose effective service rate blends toward the all-electronic-tolling (AET) rate of 1,800 veh/h as the AV fraction rises. Method. The design is a simultaneous staged taper (fan taper): at K = B - L merge stages, several lanes end simultaneously at the same x-position (staggered laterally only), so each vehicle merges at most once and no merge path crosses another lane-end. This structure was selected after the expert rejected (Exchange 2) a staged single-merge pattern that would have forced long weaving zones; the Exchange 3 counterexample identified the number of simultaneous merges at one x-position as the failure parameter, which became constraint (S). The method is sound because it separates the three objectives cleanly: geometry (length, area) is a direct function of the stage layout; throughput is governed by the booth-queue utilization and the per-lane exit demand; safety is governed by the merge-point capacity constraint, which is the dominant accident mechanism in fan-ins (concentrated merge conflicts at a single point).
tasks.mathematical_modeling_process: Variables and parameters. L = travel lanes per direction; B = tollbooths per direction, B > L; L * 2,200 veh/h = total plaza capacity C. Light demand d_light = 0.40 C, heavy demand d_heavy = 0.95 C. Booth mix of B booths: n_manual (service rate mu_manual = 350 veh/h), n_exact (mu_exact = 500 veh/h), n_etc (mu_etc = 1,200 veh/h), with n_manual + n_exact + n_etc = B. Effective per-booth service rate: mu_mix = (n_manual*350 + n_exact*500 + n_etc*1200) / B. With AV fraction alpha, effective service rate mu_eff = (1-alpha)*mu_mix + alpha*1800 (AET rate). Lane width w = 3.66 m (12 ft); free-flow speed v = 65 mph = 29.06 m/s; minimum stage spacing dx_min = 2*v = 58.1 m. Per-point merge capacity C_merge = 2,200 veh/h (one surviving lane). Merge-point constraint (S): at a stage where m lanes end and B - (cumulative merges so far) lanes survive, the flow absorbed at that point is d*m/B; the constraint is d*m/B <= C_merge, giving the maximum simultaneous merges per point m_max = floor(C_merge * B / d). Number of stages K = ceil((B - L) / m_max). Merges per stage: m_k = min(m_max, B - L - (k-1)*m_max) for k = 1..K. Stage x-positions: x_k = k * dx_min. Fan-in length: X = K*dx_min + 4*v (2 s of settling after the last stage). Paved area: A = sum over trapezoidal segments between successive stage x-positions of 0.5*(w_left + w_right)*dx, where width at a stage = (B - cumulative merges)*w_booth + remaining regular-lane widths, with w_booth = 10 m (booth egress lane width, planning figure). Throughput constraint (T): booth-queue utilization rho = d / (B * mu_eff) < 1 (M/M/c with c = B, service rate mu_eff), and d/L <= 2,200 veh/h/ln. M/M/c mean wait in queue: Wq = Lq / d, where Lq = Erlang-C(d/mu_eff, B) * rho / (1 - rho), and Erlang-C = P0 * (d/mu_eff)^B / (B! * (1-rho)), P0 = [sum_{n=0}^{B-1} (d/mu)^n / n! + (d/mu)^B / (B! (1-rho))]^{-1}. AV effect: alpha in [0,1] reduces rho linearly toward the all-AET value; the AV fraction required to restore feasibility at heavy traffic when the base mix is infeasible is found by bisection on alpha in [0,1]. Break-even for the expert-identified failure parameter: m_max drops from 2 to 1 when d exceeds d_be = C_merge * B / 2; the break-even fraction of capacity is d_be / C.
tasks.subtask_outcome_analysis: Base configuration L = 3, B = 8, booth mix {manual: 2, exact: 3, etc: 3}, capacity C = 6,600 veh/h, light = 2,640 veh/h, heavy = 6,270 veh/h. Light traffic, alpha = 0: rho = 0.455, m_max = 5, K = 1 stage (all 5 merges simultaneous), fan-in length 174 m, area 6,683 m^2, exit per lane 880 veh/h, feasible. Heavy traffic, alpha = 0: rho = infinity (d = 6,270 > B*mu_mix = 8*512.5 = 4,100), infeasible at the booth — the plaza itself cannot pass heavy demand with this mix; m_max = 2, K = 3 stages (merges per stage [2, 2, 1]), fan-in length 291 m, area 12,495 m^2. Heavy traffic, alpha = 0.5: rho = 0.621, feasible; fan-in geometry unchanged (length 291 m, area 12,495 m^2). Heavy traffic, alpha = 1.0: rho = 0.435, feasible. The AV fraction required to restore feasibility at heavy traffic with the base mix is alpha = 0.10. Second configuration L = 3, B = 12, mix {manual: 3, exact: 4, etc: 5}: heavy traffic alpha = 0: rho = 0.693, m_max = 4, K = 3, length 291 m, area 14,819 m^2, feasible; break-even fraction of capacity 2.0. Third configuration L = 4, B = 10, mix {manual: 3, exact: 4, etc: 3}: heavy traffic alpha = 0: infeasible at the booth (rho = infinity); alpha = 0.5: rho = 0.656, feasible; alpha = 1.0: rho = 0.464, feasible; break-even fraction 1.25. Sensitivity (bias axis per expert counterexample — simultaneous merges per stage vs per-point merge capacity): for L = 3, B = 8 the break-even demand at which m_max drops from 2 to 1 is d_be = 8,800 veh/h = 1.33 C, i.e. the failure mode is not triggered at any physically reachable loading for this configuration; forcing one merge per stage (the failure mode) would increase fan-in length from 291 m to 407 m, a ratio of 1.4, and area proportionally. The fan-in geometry (length and area) is insensitive to the AV fraction and to light vs heavy traffic at a fixed (L, B); what the AV fraction and booth mix govern is the booth-queue utilization and hence the feasibility of the plaza as a whole, not the fan-in shape. Limitations. (1) The merge-point capacity C_merge = 2,200 veh/h is taken as the HCM lane capacity anchor; in practice, merge capacity is lower than free-flow lane capacity, so the true break-even demand is lower than reported — the model is optimistic on safety. (2) The M/M/c booth model assumes exponential service times; exact-change booths have more variable service times, which would raise the true queue length. (3) The bounded-corridor assumption (corridor width fixed at barrier egress width) is a planning simplification; a wider flare at the barrier could reduce the fan-in length. (4) The AV headway reduction is modeled as a linear blend of service rates; connected-coordination effects (tighter merge spacing, coordinated merges) are not captured and could allow shorter stage spacing. (5) The conflict-count safety constraint is replaced by the merge-point capacity constraint; a full criticality-weighted conflict count (simple merge vs weave vs double merge) would refine the safety bound. (6) Cost is proxied by paved area only; right-of-way acquisition cost, signage, and signal infrastructure are not separately priced.
